| Organic compounds | Inorganic compounds |
|---|---|
| 1. Generally, organic compounds must have carbon. Example: Methane ($CH_4$) | 1. Except some exceptions, generally inorganic compounds have no carbon. Example: Hydrogen Sulphide ($H_2S$) |
| 2. Usually, organic compounds take a long time to react. | 2. Usually, inorganic compounds take lesser time to react. |
| 3. Organic compounds are generally formed by covalent bonding. | 3. Inorganic compounds are usually formed by ionic or covalent bonding. |

**Activity:** Define organic compounds. Taking some organic and inorganic compounds determine their melting points and show the differences.

**Think:** How to differentiate between organic and inorganic compounds on the basis of difference of ionic and covalent compounds.
